title: Fee Review Determination: Grounds and Gates for Refunding a Personal Checking Charge
content:
A refund of a Personal Checking charge is recorded against the charge it refunds. There are two refund grounds, checked in this order.

**Bank error.** A bank-error refund applies where the charge was assessed contrary to this charter — a maintenance charge in a cycle where a waiver was met, an overdraft charge beyond the tier's daily count, on an item at or below the tier's item floor, or on a day within the tier's day floor, or a charge at an amount other than the tier's own figure. A bank-error refund has no time limit and does not count toward any goodwill allowance.

**Goodwill.** A goodwill refund is a refund of a correctly assessed charge and is allowed only when every goodwill gate holds.

1. *Eligible charge.* The charge must be one of: the monthly maintenance charge, the paper statement charge, the charge for an item paid into overdraft, the charge for an item returned unpaid, the one-time charge on a prolonged negative balance, the overdraft protection transfer charge, or the domestic out-of-network cash machine charge.
2. *Posting window.* The charge must have posted no more than the tier's window of calendar days before the goodwill refund is granted. Count calendar days with the day after the charge's posted date as day 1; the refund is allowed while the frozen date is on or before that posted date plus the tier's window.
3. *Rolling allowance.* The customer's count of goodwill refunds in the rolling 365 calendar days must be below the tier's allowance, counted across all of the customer's checking accounts, each refunded charge counting as one.
4. *Account status.* The account's status must be active when a goodwill refund is granted.
5. *Once only.* A charge can be refunded at most once, the charge itself identifying the refund.

Where several charges are eligible and the allowance admits fewer than were asked for, the most recently posted charges are refunded first, and among charges posted the same day the larger charge first. The tier used for the allowance and the window is the one the account carries on the frozen date. A refund on a finally decided claim is written under the electronic claims basis and is not a goodwill refund. Requests to refund interest, charged-off balances or another bank's charges are outside this basis.

**Clauses no longer in force.** Two clauses of the opening sentence have been superseded by the current charter and are recorded here only so that no reader applies them: the clause requiring that a refund be made in full and never in part is **no longer in force**, and the clause setting the refunded amount equal to the amount of the charge it refunds is **no longer in force**. Neither may be used to work out what a refund comes to. The grounds, the gates, the ordering and the once-only rule above all stand.

**Boundary case (hypothetical).** On a tier whose window is 60 calendar days, a charge that posted 60 calendar days before the frozen date is still inside the window, because the comparison is not-later-than and the boundary day satisfies it; a charge that posted 61 calendar days before it is outside.

superseded_clauses: A fee is refunded in full, never in part
whose amount equals that fee's amount
